summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants was admitted due to worsening fatigue, shortness of breath, and generalized pruritus. Evaluation revealed an elevated BNP and a small left pleural effusion, consistent with an acute exacerbation of heart failure. She was treated with IV furosemide, which improved her symptoms. A pharmacologic stress test showed mild systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 41% and no evidence of ischemia. The cause of her pruritus remained unclear but was not associated with rash or infection. Given her immunocompromised status, she was discharged early on increased oral furosemide (80 mg twice daily) to reduce hospital-acquired infection risk. She was instructed to follow up with her cardiologist to manage her newly identified systolic dysfunction.
